body: Album wire is additive: hub announces Registered.albums, agent adds FileOffer.parts only to such a hub, final FileAnswer carries per-file parts; no new message type (ingress forwards an explicit list) and no VERSION bump. Old hub: agent sends the paths one by one.

One transfer carries a whole album (bytes concatenated, parts give sizes) instead of per-file offers regrouped on the hub, because the hub keeps one upload per connection; an album is capped at files::MAX_UPLOAD bytes (the hub file budget), so the agent splits larger sets into several albums. Alternative rejected: raise MAX_FILE_BYTES.
send_file schema lists path and paths without required/oneOf (the Messages API refuses oneOf at the top of input_schema); Server::send_file enforces exactly one, paths 2..=10.

A photo album Telegram refuses (is_photo_refusal, the group fails as a whole) is resent as a document album inside the same Op::SendAlbum job, one message token, mirroring SendPhoto; a kind with a single file goes via SendPhoto/SendDocument since sendMediaGroup needs 2-10.

Verdict SHIP rather than NEEDS_WORK: MAX_QUEUED_MESSAGES +1 overshoot and album capability captured at enqueue (stale after a hub downgrade) are minor; no loss/corruption path found in part framing (sizes come from in-memory bytes, album_fits guards slicing).

Album capability is a watch::Receiver<bool> read inside transfer() after the drain of earlier Upload events, not captured at enqueue; a multi-file group on a hub without albums returns Transfer::NoAlbum and send_group sends each file alone. Alternative rejected: reading the flag before the drain (review's verbatim fix) leaves a race where the Lost of a reconnect is drained and the album offer lands on an older hub.

Message cap for albums: the offer reserves 2 messages (kinds are known only from bytes), completion checks the exact ops count and answers Busy before any hand-off. Alternative rejected: gate only at completion, which would accept an offer whose bytes can never be sent.
